l-parked`/`--prd-coverage`-vs-`--no-prd` above are derived; gated on the same whole-lifecycle structural git-only signal used throughout the suite — no resolving tracker MCP for the run's lifecycle, asserted once, never re-sniffed per wave, the `merge-gate --local` idiom; the consult call and its verdict branch above are reused unchanged):** derive emptiness via `faff queue-state derive` (pure) — on exit 0 with a parseable `{queue_empty, all_parked}`, include `--queue-empty`/`--all-parked` only when each boolean is `true` (omit for `false`, never a negative flag); on any non-zero exit, or an unparseable/missing-field result, omit **both** flags — `run-done` then reads `queue_empty:false, all_parked:false` → `work-remaining` → `continue`, exactly today's safe default, never `run-complete` (log the fault to the wave log; never hard-stop on it). For the PRD floor: when no checklist PRD is in scope for this run (the same "unless a PRD is in scope" determination already gating `--no-prd` above — reused as-is, no new resolver introduced), pass `--no-prd`; when one is in scope, run `faff prd-checklist <prd-path>` and, on exit 0 with a block carrying a boolean `.satisfied`, pass `--prd-coverage '<that block>'` — otherwise (non-zero exit, unparseable, or a missing/non-boolean `.satisfied`) pass `--no-prd` instead, never fabricating `.satisfied`/`.covered`; pass **exactly one** of `--prd-coverage`/`--no-prd`, never both (`run-done` silently ignores `--prd-coverage` whenever `--no-prd` is also present, nulling a satisfied PRD). `--ledger-clean`/`--budget`/`--non-convergence`/`--policy` are assembled identically to the tracker path above — no git-only variant. Pass the derived `--prd-coverage`/`--budget`/`--policy` values to `faff run-done` as single argv elements, never spliced into a shell command string — a checklist PRD is attacker-shapeable repo content, and `run-done`'s own boolean-`.satisfied` pre-validation bounds, but does not replace, this argv discipline.

   **Capture the wave-boundary decisions (best-effort, `FAFF_RUN_DIR`-guarded; per issue `__run__`).** Run the `faff run-done` consult through the driver in one command, `eval "$(faff decision-capture decide --run <run> --issue __run__ --kernel run-done --wave <w> --export)" && faff run-done …`; after its verdict branch emit `faff decision-capture action --run <run> --issue __run__ --kernel run-done --wave <w> --action <the wave-boundary verdict taken>` (the run-termination vocabulary, `faff contract run-termination --describe`), with the **same `<w>`** on both calls (wave-consistency: a mismatched `--wave` re-derives a different id and breaks the join). `queue-state` is Tier-2 mint-and-silence: run the `faff queue-state derive` read as `eval "$(faff decision-capture decide --run <run> --issue __run__ --kernel queue-state --export)" && faff queue-state derive …` only; the minted id silences the empty-id note, and it emits **no** action marker (a rollup with no single downstream action).

Log each wave's admissions, drain count, `filed_this_wave`, `no_progress_waves`, the `run-done` verdict (whenever it was consulted — the L3 default, L4, or any git-only run; i.e. every run except an opted-out L3 tracker run), the `faff sentry check` intervention (every run — the consult is advisory except where the run acts on `abort` (run-stop) or `pause` (parks the implicated issue, continues): an unattended run, i.e. L4 or an L3 that declared `autonomous.unattended` / the `sentry_acting` alias), and exit reason under `.faff/runs/<run-id>/wave-N/`. Exit reasons are `drained` (queue empty after build pass), `all-parked` (every remaining issue parked or errored), `budget-hit` (budget gate fired during or at the boundary of this wave), `sentry-abort` (a sentry `abort` intervention fired and the run acted on it — an unattended run: L4, or an L3 with `autonomous.unattended` / the `sentry_acting` alias), or — whenever the `run-done` consult ran (the L3 default, L4, or any git-only run) — `converged/both-dry` and `non-convergence` (the run-done verdicts above).

**Why this exists:** chains unlocked mid-run (`ISSUE-A` ships → `ISSUE-B`'s blocker clears) are picked up here. The chain's downstream items live in Backlog (per the promotion rule above), which is why prep is the entry point — the orchestrator does not move state directly. Chains visible at first assembly are still handled by step 5's conflict analysis as collision groups — wave re-entry catches the rest.

### 9. Wave-1 empty short-circuit

If wave 1's build queue is empty after assembly (step 4), skip steps 5–8 and proceed directly to reporting. No subsequent waves run — there's nothing for shipped work to chain on. Prep output still counts as a successful run.

### 10. File discovered-scope tickets

After the wave loop converges (and only when builds ran — the wave-1 short-circuit at step 9 skips this), collect the **discovered scope** `/faff-graft` recorded during the run and file the concrete items as Backlog tickets. This is bottom-up source (b) — execution-discovered work (gateway → **Agent Lanes**). It is the one step where beep-boop writes tickets **directly** rather than via tidy — legitimately, as the orchestrator lane (full tracker write). **Same procedure, up to three timings** (file-and-defer is the **fallback** whenever the loop is opted out (L3) or budget-capped — no discovered scope is ever dropped):
- **L4:** sub-steps 1–7 fire **per build return at step 7** (eager, the primary filer) and again **per wave at step 8.0** as an idempotent reconcile/backstop (already-filed items dedup-skip); this end-of-run pass files only the true residual (final-wave scope, or a budget-breach short-circuit).
- **L3, convergence loop on (not opted out):** the same sub-steps run **per wave at step 8.0** only (no step-7 eager filing — that's L4-only) so scope re-enters the same run; this end-of-run pass again files only the residual.
- **Opted-out L3 run:** the loop is off entirely (no step 7, no step 8.
